Annual meeting 2024 – Obstacles and Incentives for Gas Monetisation and Emissions Management

Sep 2024Dr Valérie Marcel

2024 Annual Meeting: Summary and analysis

Paramaribo, 3-4 June 2024

Staatsolie hosted the 2024 Annual meeting in Paramaribo, Suriname. It brought together governments, NOCs, industry partners, and technical experts for a two-day international discussion, as well as training.

Key messages

  • The New Producers for Sustainable Energy 2024 annual meeting addressed the challenges and opportunities faced by emerging producers in developing natural gas resources and managing greenhouse gas emissions.
  • The global investment mood in oil and gas is bullish, but capital expenditure is unevenly distributed, favouring North America and Latin America.
  • Equity issues are central for member countries, with the Global North discouraging new oil and gas projects in the Global South, while increasing their own production.
  • The Global South members of the NP4SE emphasised the need for energy access to alleviate poverty and drive development.
  • Lock-in risks associated with gas infrastructure investments are lower for downstream projects and can be mitigated for upstream projects by lowering costs and execution time, notably through small-scale and modular approaches.
  • Monetizing associated gas and methane presents challenges due to immature markets and infrastructure but offers significant economic and environmental benefits.
  • Growing focus on GHG emissions has led to increased pressure on operators to reduce emissions, particularly methane.
  • Financing decarbonization and gas projects remains a challenge, with limited public finance available and commercial banks hesitant to invest.
  • New producers are exploring alternative financing options, such as climate bonds and partnerships with Asian importing countries and institutions like the African Energy Bank.
